## Summary

This is `gpt-cli`, a terminal chat client that dispatches to a different SDK per model-name prefix (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Cohere, local LLaMA). I migrated the two call sites that have a Router-compatible surface and left the rest native, since Router only exposes OpenAI-Responses and Anthropic-Messages compatibility.

**Migrated:**
- **`gptcli/providers/openai.py`** — already used the Responses API (`client.responses.create`), so only the client construction changed: it now builds `OpenAI(api_key=RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY, base_url=RAMP_ROUTER_BASE_URL or https://api.router.com/v1)` instead of using the global `openai.api_key`/`openai.base_url`. All request/response handling (reasoning, streaming, tool events, usage) is untouched.
- **`gptcli/providers/azure_openai.py`** — deleted. Azure was just a differently-authenticated OpenAI client; since Router is now the single credential holder, `oai-azure:`-prefixed models route through the same Router-backed `OpenAICompletionProvider` (dispatch in `assistant.py` updated accordingly).
- **`gptcli/providers/anthropic.py`** — per the instructions, code already on the Anthropic Messages API doesn't need rewriting to Responses. I only repointed the `anthropic.Anthropic` client at Router's `/v1/messages` surface (`api_key=RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`, `base_url` = Router base **without** the trailing `/v1`, since the Anthropic SDK appends `/v1/messages` itself — confirmed this by hand against the Router simulator, which 404'd until I stripped it).
- **`gptcli/config.py` / `gptcli/gpt.py`** — removed `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and the Azure API-version setting, along with the per-assistant `openai_base_url_override`/`openai_api_key_override` escape hatch (that let an assistant send an arbitrary API key to an arbitrary endpoint, which conflicts with "the application must never send provider API keys").
- Verified end-to-end against the Router simulator with a single text-only request on each migrated path — both returned valid `pong` responses with usage data before I ran the full suite (14/14 pass, unaffected since they mock the provider layer).
- Updated README to describe `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` instead of the removed provider keys/overrides.

**Could not migrate (left on native provider SDKs, call sites unchanged):**
- **`gptcli/providers/google.py`** (Gemini) and **`gptcli/providers/cohere.py`** — both use proprietary non-OpenAI, non-Anthropic request/response schemas. Router only documents OpenAI-Responses and Anthropic-Messages compatibility surfaces, so migrating these would mean guessing whether/how Router exposes Gemini or Cohere models and under what model ID, which the instructions explicitly forbid ("never invent one or reuse a provider's public model name"). Their native API keys (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `COHERE_API_KEY`) are intentionally left in `config.py` since they're still required.
- **`gptcli/providers/llama.py`** — runs `llama_cpp` in-process against a local model file; there's no network call at all, so there's nothing to route through Router.
